claim: The Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes are the main microtubule binding components of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae kinetochore.
source: The Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes are the main microtubule binding components of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae kinetochore.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction as an established fact about yeast kinetochore composition.

claim: Cooperation between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes enhances kinetochore-microtubule coupling.
source: Cooperation between these two complexes enhances kinetochore-microtubule coupling and is regulated by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Lampert et al., 2010, 2013; Tien et al., 2010) mentioned in the introduction.

claim: The interaction between Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes is regulated by Aurora B kinase.
source: Cooperation between these two complexes enhances kinetochore-microtubule coupling and is regulated by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Lampert et al., 2013; Tien et al., 2010).

claim: The Ndc80 complex can simultaneously bind and bridge across two Dam1 complex rings through a tripartite interaction.
source: We show that the Ndc80 complex can simultaneously bind and bridge across two Dam1 complex rings through a tripartite interaction, each component of which is regulated by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cross-linking mass spectrometry data (Figure 1A), TIRF microscopy experiments (Figure 1D, Figure 2), and electron microscopy (Figure 3).

claim: Each component of the tripartite interaction between Ndc80 and Dam1 complexes is regulated by Aurora B kinase.
source: We show that the Ndc80 complex can simultaneously bind and bridge across two Dam1 complex rings through a tripartite interaction, each component of which is regulated by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This is supported by selective phosphorylation experiments shown in Figure 2 demonstrating that phosphorylation of different combinations of sites affects the interaction.

claim: Mutations in any one of the Ndc80p interaction regions abrogates the Ndc80 complex's ability to bind two Dam1 rings in vitro.
source: Mutations in any one of the Ndc80p interaction regions abrogates the Ndc80 complex's ability to bind two Dam1 rings in vitro, and results in kinetochore biorientation and microtubule attachment defects in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing that mutations in regions A, B, or C prevent the characteristic 33 nm Dam1 ring spacing (Figure 3—figure supplements 1D–F and 2).

claim: Mutations in Ndc80p interaction regions result in kinetochore biorientation defects in vivo.
source: Mutations in any one of the Ndc80p interaction regions abrogates the Ndc80 complex's ability to bind two Dam1 rings in vitro, and results in kinetochore biorientation and microtubule attachment defects in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data showing monooriented and detached CEN3 in mutant cells (Figure 5A,B).

claim: Mutations in Ndc80p interaction regions result in microtubule attachment defects in vivo.
source: Mutations in any one of the Ndc80p interaction regions abrogates the Ndc80 complex's ability to bind two Dam1 rings in vitro, and results in kinetochore biorientation and microtubule attachment defects in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging showing detached kinetochores and reduced Dam1 complex localization at kinetochores (Figures 5 and 6).

claim: An extra-long Ndc80 complex, engineered to space the two Dam1 rings further apart, does not support growth.
source: We also show that an extra-long Ndc80 complex, engineered to space the two Dam1 rings further apart, does not support growth.
evidence: This is supported by plasmid shuffle assay showing that ndc8010hep and nuf210hep together cannot support viability (Figure 4A).

claim: Each kinetochore in vivo contains two Dam1 rings.
source: Taken together, our work suggests that each kinetochore in vivo contains two Dam1 rings and that proper spacing between the rings is vital.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of in vitro data showing Ndc80 bridges two rings, the lethality of mutations that prevent two-ring binding, and the lethality of altered ring spacing.

claim: Proper spacing between Dam1 rings is vital for kinetochore function.
source: Taken together, our work suggests that each kinetochore in vivo contains two Dam1 rings and that proper spacing between the rings is vital.
evidence: This is supported by the lethality of the Ndc8010hep complex which increases ring spacing by 9 nm (Figures 3 and 4).

claim: Strong kinetochore-microtubule attachments are essential for faithful segregation of sister chromatids during mitosis.
source: Strong kinetochore-microtubule attachments are essential for faithful segregation of sister chromatids during mitosis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The Ndc80 complex connects the Dam1 complex to the rest of the kinetochore.
source: The Ndc80 complex connects the Dam1 complex to the rest of the kinetochore.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes interact on microtubules, significantly increasing the strength of Ndc80 complex attachment to microtubules.
source: The two complexes interact on microtubules, significantly increasing the strength of Ndc80 complex attachment to microtubules (Lampert et al., 2010, 2013; Tien et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is a scaffold for the spindle assembly checkpoint.
source: The Ndc80 complex is a scaffold for the spindle assembly checkpoint (Dou et al., 2015; Hiruma et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Both the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes are targets of Aurora B kinase.
source: Both the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes are targets of Aurora B kinase, which corrects aberrant kinetochore-microtubule attachments to achieve bioriented attachments (Reviewed in Sarangapani and Asbury, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a review citation.

claim: Aurora B kinase phosphorylation of Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p together disrupts the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes.
source: Aurora B kinase phosphorylation of the Dam1 complex components Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p together disrupts the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes (Lampert et al., 2013; Tien et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The Dam1 complex spontaneously assembles into microtubule-encircling rings in vitro.
source: The spontaneous assembly in vitro of the Dam1 complex into microtubule-encircling rings suggests a compelling mechanism for kinetochore-microtubule coupling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with implicit reference to prior work.

claim: Oligomerization of the Dam1 complex is essential for formation of strong kinetochore-microtubule attachments.
source: We don't know the organization of the Dam1 complex in the cell, although oligomerization is essential for formation of strong kinetochore-microtubule attachments (McIntosh et al., 2013; Umbreit et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Estimates of the number of Dam1 complexes at the kinetochore in vivo range from as low as 10 to as high as 32.
source: Estimates of the number of Dam1 complexes at the kinetochore in vivo have suggested numbers as low as 10, which is not enough to form a single 16-membered ring, and as high as 32, which is enough for two rings (Aravamudhan et al., 2013; Joglekar et al., 2006; Lawrimore et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous counting studies.

claim: Previous budding yeast kinetochore models have assumed one Dam1 complex ring.
source: Despite this uncertainty, previous budding yeast kinetochore models have assumed one Dam1 complex ring (Aravamudhan et al., 2015; Cheeseman and Desai, 2008; Joglekar et al., 2009; Tanaka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: The C-terminal regions of Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p form cross-links to three distinct regions of Ndc80p.
source: The C-terminal regions of Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p formed cross-links to three distinct regions of Ndc80p (Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by cross-linking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The C-terminal regions of Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p include five sites phosphorylated by Aurora B kinase.
source: These three C-terminal regions of the Dam1 complex include five sites phosphorylated by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A with yellow lines indicating phosphorylation sites.

claim: Phosphorylation of all five Aurora B kinase sites on Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p fully disrupts the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes.
source: Phosphorylation of all five sites fully disrupts the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes (Lampert et al., 2010; Tien et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and confirmed by data in Figure 2A.

claim: Three regions on Ndc80p map near or within regions that cross-link to Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p.
source: Three of these regions map near or within the regions that cross-link to Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown by comparing cross-linking data with functional regions identified by linker-scanning mutagenesis (Tien et al., 2013).

claim: Lethal mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p partially disrupt the Ndc80 complex's interaction with Dam1 complex.
source: However, addition of the Dam1 complex only partially increased the residence time of the mutant complexes as compared to the wild-type Ndc80 complex (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data showing reduced residence times for mutant Ndc80 complexes in the presence of Dam1 complex (Figure 1D).

claim: The presence of the Dam1 complex significantly increases the residence time of wild-type Ndc80 complex on microtubules.
source: As reported previously, the presence of the Dam1 complex significantly increases the residence time of wild-type Ndc80 complex on microtubules (Tien et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and confirmed by data in Figure 1D.

claim: Mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p do not alter the residence time of the Ndc80 complex alone on microtubules.
source: These mutations also did not alter the residence time of the Ndc80 complex alone on microtubules, consistent with previous observations (Tien et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data (Figure 1D) and citation to previous work.

claim: Aurora B kinase phosphorylates the Dam1 complex at six different sites: Dam1p S20, S257, S265, S292; Ask1p S200; Spc34p T199.
source: Aurora B kinase phosphorylates the Dam1 complex at six different sites: Dam1p S20, S257, S265, S292; Ask1p S200; Spc34p T199 (Cheeseman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Phosphorylation of Dam1p S20 significantly decreases Dam1 complex oligomerization.
source: Phosphorylation of Dam1p S20 significantly decreases Dam1 complex oligomerization, while phosphorylation of the three C-terminal sites in Dam1p slightly inhibits direct binding of the Dam1 complex to microtubules (Gestaut et al., 2008; Zelter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Phosphorylation of the three C-terminal sites in Dam1p slightly inhibits direct binding of the Dam1 complex to microtubules.
source: Phosphorylation of Dam1p S20 significantly decreases Dam1 complex oligomerization, while phosphorylation of the three C-terminal sites in Dam1p slightly inhibits direct binding of the Dam1 complex to microtubules (Gestaut et al., 2008; Zelter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Simultaneously phosphorylating all three regions ADam1p, BAsk1p, and CSpc34p completely disrupts the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes.
source: Simultaneously phosphorylating all three regions, ADam1p, BAsk1p, and CSpc34p completely disrupted the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes, as reported previously (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Tien et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data (Figure 2A) and citation to previous work.

claim: Individually phosphorylating regions ADam1p, BAsk1p, or CSpc34p causes only partial disruption of the Dam1-Ndc80 interaction.
source: Individually phosphorylating regions ADam1p, BAsk1p, or CSpc34p caused only partial disruption.
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Phosphorylating region BAsk1p together with CSpc34p only partially disrupts the Dam1-Ndc80 interaction.
source: Phosphorylating region BAsk1p together with CSpc34p also only partially disrupted the interaction
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Phosphorylating ADam1p in combination with either BAsk1p or CSpc34p is sufficient to fully disrupt the Dam1-Ndc80 interaction.
source: but phosphorylating ADam1p in combination with either BAsk1p or CSpc34p was sufficient to fully disrupt the interaction (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The coiled-coiled length between regions ANdc80p and CNdc80p is predicted to be 29 nm.
source: The coiled-coiled length between regions ANdc80p and CNdc80p is predicted to be 29 nm (Lupas and Gruber, 2005) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on coiled-coil prediction software cited in the text.

claim: The width of a Dam1 complex ring is approximately 7 nm.
source: The width of a Dam1 complex ring is only ~7 nm (Ramey et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous structural work.

claim: In the absence of the Ndc80 complex, Dam1 complex rings bind in doublets at an inter-ring distance of 13.3 ± 2.4 nm.
source: In the absence of the Ndc80 complex, the Dam1 complex rings tended to bind in doublets of rings, at an inter-ring distance of 13.3 ± 2.4 nm (avg ± s.d.) (Figure 3A–C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Dam1 complex rings have an affinity for each other along the longitudinal axis of microtubules.
source: This suggests that Dam1 complex rings have an affinity for each other along the longitudinal axis of microtubules and have a tendency to stack together.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of ring doublets in the absence of Ndc80 complex.

claim: In the presence of the Ndc80 complex, 49.1% of Dam1 ring pairs are found in closely spaced doublets.
source: The percent of Dam1 ring pairs found in closely spaced doublets was higher in the presence of the Ndc80 complex, 49.1% (estimated by Gaussian fitting to the peak, see Materials and methods), as compared to without the Ndc80 complex, 18.8%.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data and Gaussian fitting analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the absence of the Ndc80 complex, 18.8% of Dam1 ring pairs are found in closely spaced doublets.
source: The percent of Dam1 ring pairs found in closely spaced doublets was higher in the presence of the Ndc80 complex, 49.1% (estimated by Gaussian fitting to the peak, see Materials and methods), as compared to without the Ndc80 complex, 18.8%.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data and Gaussian fitting analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the presence of wild-type Ndc80 complex, Dam1 rings in doublets are separated by a distance of 33.1 ± 3.8 nm.
source: In addition, the two rings in each doublet were consistently held apart by a distance of 33.1 ± 3.8 nm, similar to the predicted coiled-coil length between regions ANdc80p and CNdc80p (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: One Ndc80 complex bridges two Dam1 rings by binding one ring at region ANdc80p and a second ring at region CNdc80p.
source: This suggests that one Ndc80 complex bridges two Dam1 rings by binding one ring at region ANdc80p and a second ring at region CNdc80p.
evidence: This is inferred from the 33 nm spacing matching the predicted distance between regions A and C on Ndc80p.

claim: In the presence of the Ndc8010-hep complex, Dam1 ring doublets are separated by 42.1 ± 2.1 nm.
source: In the presence of the 10-heptad mutant Ndc80 (Ndc8010-hep) complex, Dam1 ring doublets were consistently separated by 42.1 ± 2.1 nm, 9 nm farther apart than in the presence of wild-type Ndc80 complex (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The Ndc8010-hep complex separates Dam1 rings 9 nm farther apart than wild-type Ndc80 complex.
source: In the presence of the 10-heptad mutant Ndc80 (Ndc8010-hep) complex, Dam1 ring doublets were consistently separated by 42.1 ± 2.1 nm, 9 nm farther apart than in the presence of wild-type Ndc80 complex (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is calculated from the difference between 42.1 nm and 33.1 nm measurements.

claim: Mutation in regions A, B or C of Ndc80p abolishes its ability to bind two rings.
source: Finally, mutation in regions A, B or C of Ndc80p abolished its ability to bind two rings as the Dam1 inter-ring distance in these cases was the same in the absence of Ndc80 complex (Figure 3—figure supplements 1D–F and and 2).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing that mutant Ndc80 complexes do not change Dam1 ring spacing from the no-Ndc80 control.

claim: The ndc8010hep and nuf210hep alleles together cannot support growth.
source: Using a plasmid shuffle assay, we found that even when introduced together, ndc8010hep and nuf210hep could not support growth, even though the encoded proteins were expressed (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by plasmid shuffle assay data (Figure 4A) and western blot showing protein expression (Figure 4B).

claim: The Ndc8010hep complex is competent to assemble in vitro.
source: The Ndc8010hep complex is competent to assemble in vitro, to bind microtubules, to interact with the Dam1 complex on microtubules, and to bind two Dam1 complex rings (Figure 3; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data (Figure 4C) and electron microscopy data (Figure 3).

claim: The Ndc8010hep complex can bind microtubules.
source: The Ndc8010hep complex is competent to assemble in vitro, to bind microtubules, to interact with the Dam1 complex on microtubules, and to bind two Dam1 complex rings (Figure 3; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data showing microtubule residence times (Figure 4C).

claim: The Ndc8010hep complex can interact with the Dam1 complex on microtubules.
source: The Ndc8010hep complex is competent to assemble in vitro, to bind microtubules, to interact with the Dam1 complex on microtubules, and to bind two Dam1 complex rings (Figure 3; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data showing increased residence time in the presence of Dam1 complex (Figure 4C).

claim: The Ndc8010hep complex can bind two Dam1 complex rings.
source: The Ndc8010hep complex is competent to assemble in vitro, to bind microtubules, to interact with the Dam1 complex on microtubules, and to bind two Dam1 complex rings (Figure 3; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing 42 nm Dam1 ring spacing (Figure 3).

claim: The Ndc8010hep complex cannot support viability due to an altered Dam1 complex inter-ring distance.
source: These results suggest that the Ndc8010hep complex cannot support viability due to an altered Dam1 complex inter-ring distance.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that the only known difference is the increased inter-ring distance, and all other functions are intact in vitro.

claim: Cells carrying wild-type NDC80 progress through mitosis as expected.
source: Budding index analyses revealed that cells carrying wild-type NDC80 progressed through mitosis as expected.
evidence: This is supported by budding index data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cells without NDC80 bud and divide on schedule despite major defects in kinetochore attachment.
source: Cells without NDC80 also budded and divided on schedule, despite major defects in kinetochore attachment (see below), as expected since activation of the SAC requires the Ndc80 complex (Dou et al., 2015; Hiruma et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by budding index data and citations explaining that SAC requires Ndc80.

claim: Cells carrying Ndc80p mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p arrest as large-budded cells.
source: In contrast, cells carrying Ndc80p mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p arrested as large-budded cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) suggesting defects in kinetochore attachment and indicating that the checkpoint remained functional.
evidence: This is supported by budding index data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: In 78% of wild-type NDC80 cells, CEN3 is in metaphase as judged by spindle length.
source: In the majority of wild-type NDC80 cells, CEN3 was bioriented with both CEN3-GFP puncta on the spindle axis; 78% were in metaphase and 22% were in anaphase as judged by the spindle length.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In 22% of wild-type NDC80 cells, CEN3 is in anaphase as judged by spindle length.
source: In the majority of wild-type NDC80 cells, CEN3 was bioriented with both CEN3-GFP puncta on the spindle axis; 78% were in metaphase and 22% were in anaphase as judged by the spindle length.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In the majority of Ndc80-depleted cells, CEN3-GFP is off of the spindle axis, consistent with complete detachment.
source: In the majority of the Ndc80-depleted cells, CEN3-GFP was off of the spindle axis, consistent with complete detachment.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: A mutation in region ANdc80p results in 61% of cells with monooriented CEN3 and 34% of cells with detached CEN3.
source: A mutation in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p, resulted in 61, 59, and 75% of the cells with monooriented CEN3 and 34, 39, and 21% of cells with detached CEN3, respectively. (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A mutation in region BNdc80p results in 59% of cells with monooriented CEN3 and 39% of cells with detached CEN3.
source: A mutation in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p, resulted in 61, 59, and 75% of the cells with monooriented CEN3 and 34, 39, and 21% of cells with detached CEN3, respectively. (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A mutation in region CNdc80p results in 75% of cells with monooriented CEN3 and 21% of cells with detached CEN3.
source: A mutation in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p, resulted in 61, 59, and 75% of the cells with monooriented CEN3 and 34, 39, and 21% of cells with detached CEN3, respectively. (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Ndc80p carrying a mutation in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p disrupts kinetochore biorientation in vivo.
source: Thus, we conclude that Ndc80p carrying a mutation in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p disrupts kinetochore biorientation and attachment in vivo.
evidence: This is concluded from the live cell imaging data showing monooriented and detached kinetochores (Figure 5).

claim: Ndc80p carrying a mutation in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p disrupts kinetochore attachment in vivo.
source: Thus, we conclude that Ndc80p carrying a mutation in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p disrupts kinetochore biorientation and attachment in vivo.
evidence: This is concluded from the live cell imaging data showing detached kinetochores (Figure 5).

claim: The Ndc80 complex is responsible for recruiting the Dam1 complex to the kinetochore.
source: The Ndc80 complex is responsible for recruiting the Dam1 complex to the kinetochore (Janke et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cells expressing wild-type NDC80 have two distinct clusters of Mtw1-YFP between two SPBs.
source: Cells expressing wild-type NDC80 had two distinct clusters of Mtw1-YFP between two SPBs, as expected for bioriented sister kinetochores.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In wild-type cells, the Dam1 complex localizes along the spindle and shows two distinct clusters that colocalize with Mtw1-YFP.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Cheeseman et al., 2001; Hofmann et al., 1998; Li et al., 2002), the Dam1 complex localized along the spindle but also showed two distinct clusters that colocalized with the Mtw1-YFP. (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data (Figure 6A,B) and citations to previous work.

claim: In mutant Ndc80 cells, Dad4-CFP decorates the spindle but concentrates poorly at the Mtw1-YFP clusters.
source: Unlike wild-type NDC80, Dad4-CFP in mutant Ndc80 cells decorated the spindle but concentrated poorly at the Mtw1-YFP clusters that did occur (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging and line scan data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In wild-type NDC80 cells, an increase or decrease in Mtw1-YFP fluorescence correlates with an increase or decrease in Dad4-CFP fluorescence.
source: In wild-type NDC80 cells, an increase or decrease in Mtw1-YFP fluorescence correlated with an increase or decrease in Dad4-CFP fluorescence, respectively
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Ndc80-depleted cells show poor correlation between Mtw1-YFP and Dad4-CFP fluorescence.
source: however, Ndc80-depleted cells showed poor correlation.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: One or multiple mutations in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p result in significantly decreased correlation between Mtw1-YFP and Dad4-CFP.
source: One or multiple mutations in region ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p resulted in significantly decreased correlation between Mtw1-YFP and Dad4-CFP (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p disrupt the ability of Ndc80 to recruit Dam1 complex to the kinetochore in vivo.
source: These observations suggest that mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p had little effect on binding of Dam1 complex to the microtubules, but disrupted the ability of Ndc80 to recruit Dam1 complex to the kinetochore in vivo, thereby causing severe defects in kinetochore attachment and biorientation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Dam1 decorates spindles but doesn't concentrate at kinetochores in mutant cells.

claim: Rings are not required for the Dam1 complex to track depolymerizing microtubules in the absence of tension.
source: Rings are not required for the Dam1 complex to track depolymerizing microtubules in the absence of tension (Gestaut et al., 2008; Grishchuk et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Oligomerization of the Dam1 complex is required to maintain attachments under tension.
source: However, oligomerization of the Dam1 complex is required to maintain attachments under tension as would be experienced during metaphase (Umbreit et al., 2014; Volkov et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Prior models of the kinetochore have all assumed that each kinetochore contains only one Dam1 complex ring.
source: Prior models of the kinetochore have all assumed that each kinetochore contains only one Dam1 complex ring.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of previous modeling approaches.

claim: Faithful microtubule attachments require two Dam1 complex rings per kinetochore in vivo.
source: These results suggest that faithful microtubule attachments require two Dam1 complex rings per kinetochore in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of data showing Ndc80 bridges two rings in vitro and that mutations preventing two-ring binding cause attachment defects in vivo.

claim: Counting of kinetochore components by fluorescence microscopy has yielded conflicting results for the number of Dam1 complexes at the yeast kinetochore.
source: Counting of kinetochore components by fluorescence microscopy has yielded conflicting results for the number of Dam1 complexes at the yeast kinetochore depending on the standard used.
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies with different results.

claim: Assuming two Cse4 histone molecules per kinetochore, there are enough Dam1 complexes to form one ring at a kinetochore during metaphase.
source: Assuming two Cse4 histone molecules per kinetochore, Joglekar and coworkers report enough Dam1 complexes to form one ring at a kinetochore during metaphase and a partial ring during anaphase (Aravamudhan et al., 2013; Joglekar et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous counting studies.

claim: Lawrimore and coworkers measured 5.5 Cse4 histone molecules per kinetochore, giving enough Dam1 complex for two rings at a kinetochore during anaphase.
source: Lawrimore and coworkers measured 5.5 Cse4 histone molecules per kinetochore, giving enough Dam1 complex for two rings at a kinetochore during anaphase (Lawrimore et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous counting study.

claim: Coffman and coworkers measured 8 Cse4 histone molecules per kinetochore.
source: whereas Coffman and coworkers measured 8 Cse4 histone molecules per kinetochore (Coffman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous counting study.

claim: There are two Dam1 complex rings at the kinetochore.
source: Our results show that the Ndc80 complex can bind two Dam1 rings in vitro. Given the results of the latter two groups, we propose that there are two Dam1 complex rings at the kinetochore.
evidence: This is proposed based on the combination of in vitro data and counting studies suggesting sufficient Dam1 complexes for two rings.

claim: The region before the hairpin of Ndc80p has been identified as a binding site for the Dam1 complex.
source: The region before the hairpin and the loop region of Ndc80p have both been identified as binding sites for the Dam1 complex (Lampert et al., 2013; Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The loop region of Ndc80p has been identified as a binding site for the Dam1 complex.
source: The region before the hairpin and the loop region of Ndc80p have both been identified as binding sites for the Dam1 complex (Lampert et al., 2013; Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The interaction between the Ndc80 and Dam1 complexes forms a tripartite network.
source: Our results indicate that the interaction between the Ndc80 and Dam1 complexes is more extensive forming a tripartite network.
evidence: This is concluded from the cross-linking and functional data showing three distinct interaction regions.

claim: One of the three interaction regions between Ndc80 and Dam1 complexes is the hairpin, consistent with previous reports.
source: The C-terminal domains of Dam1p, Ask1p, and Spc34p interact with three distinct regions of Ndc80p, one of which is the hairpin consistent with the previous report (Lampert et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cross-linking data and citation to previous work.

claim: The results are consistent with a previous study showing an interaction between Ndc80p and the C-terminal region of Dam1p.
source: Our results are also consistent with a previous study showing an interaction between Ndc80p and the C-terminal region of Dam1p (Kalantzaki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: No evidence was found for an interaction between the Ndc80p 'loop' region and Dam1p.
source: However, we did not find any evidence for an interaction between the Ndc80p 'loop' region and Dam1p (Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the cross-linking data, contrasting with a previous report.

claim: Regions A and B contribute to the Ndc80 complex interaction with the ring closer to the N-terminus of Ndc80p/Nuf2p.
source: Comparing the predicted distances between regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p, and the 33 nm Dam1 complex inter-ring distance from EM experiments suggests that regions A and B contribute to the Ndc80 complex interaction with the ring closer to the N-terminus of Ndc80p/Nuf2p, while region C contributes to the Ndc80 complex interaction with the second ring (Figure 7).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing predicted coiled-coil distances with measured inter-ring distances.

claim: Region C contributes to the Ndc80 complex interaction with the second Dam1 ring further from the Ndc80p N-terminus.
source: Comparing the predicted distances between regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p, and the 33 nm Dam1 complex inter-ring distance from EM experiments suggests that regions A and B contribute to the Ndc80 complex interaction with the ring closer to the N-terminus of Ndc80p/Nuf2p, while region C contributes to the Ndc80 complex interaction with the second ring (Figure 7).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing predicted coiled-coil distances with measured inter-ring distances.

claim: Disrupting interaction A is more severe than disrupting interaction B or C.
source: Our TIRF microscopy and live cell imaging results suggest that disrupting interaction A is more severe than disrupting interaction B or C.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the effects of different mutations in TIRF and live cell experiments (Figures 1, 2, 5, 6).

claim: A computational model positions region ADam1p and BAsk1p near the microtubule surface.
source: A recent computational model of the structure of the Dam1 complex bound to microtubules positions region ADam1p and BAsk1p near the microtubule surface, while region CSpc34p is positioned away from the microtubule surface (Zelter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous computational modeling work.

claim: A computational model positions region CSpc34p away from the microtubule surface.
source: A recent computational model of the structure of the Dam1 complex bound to microtubules positions region ADam1p and BAsk1p near the microtubule surface, while region CSpc34p is positioned away from the microtubule surface (Zelter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous computational modeling work.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is positioned under the first Dam1 ring and above the second Dam1 complex ring further from Ndc80p N-terminus.
source: Accordingly, our model of the interaction between Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes shows the Ndc80 complex positioned under the first Dam1 ring and above the second Dam1 complex ring further from Ndc80p N-terminus (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the structural constraints from cross-linking, distance measurements, and previous computational models.

claim: Aberrant kinetochore-microtubule attachments are phosphorylated and destabilized by Aurora B kinase.
source: Aberrant kinetochore-microtubule attachments are phosphorylated and destabilized by Aurora B kinase (Biggins et al., 1999; Cheeseman et al., 2002; Hauf et al., 2003; Pinsky et al., 2006; Tanaka et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Phosphorylation of certain combinations of Dam1 complex sites results in only partial disruption of the Dam1-Ndc80 interaction.
source: We show that phosphorylation of certain combinations results in only partial disruption and full disruption does not require phosphorylation of all three proteins.
evidence: This is supported by the selective phosphorylation experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Full disruption of the Dam1-Ndc80 interaction does not require phosphorylation of all three proteins.
source: We show that phosphorylation of certain combinations results in only partial disruption and full disruption does not require phosphorylation of all three proteins.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that phosphorylation of ADam1p plus either BAsk1p or CSpc34p is sufficient for full disruption (Figure 2B).

claim: Aurora B kinase can fine tune the interaction between Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes, resulting in a range of disruption.
source: Our results suggest how the Aurora B kinase might fine tune the interaction between Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes, resulting in a range of disruption.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that different phosphorylation combinations produce different levels of disruption.

claim: The transition from 13 nm to 33 nm Dam1 complex inter-ring distance could signal the establishment of kinetochore-microtubule attachment or biorientation.
source: The transition from 13 nm, in the absence of the Ndc80 complex, to 33 nm Dam1 complex inter-ring distance could signal the establishment of kinetochore-microtubule attachment or biorientation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed change in ring spacing upon Ndc80 binding.

claim: Deviation from the specific 33 nm Dam1 ring distance might disrupt a yet unknown mechanism for detecting kinetochore-microtubule attachments or bioriented attachments.
source: Deviation from the specific 33 nm distance might disrupt a yet unknown mechanism for detecting kinetochore-microtubule attachments, or bioriented attachments, or both.
evidence: This is speculation about why the Ndc8010hep complex is lethal despite being functional in vitro.

claim: The presence of two Dam1 rings at the kinetochore in a specific orientation bound to the Ndc80 complex would have implications for how attachment strength is established and modulated by tension.
source: The presence of two Dam1 rings at the kinetochore, in a specific orientation bound to the Ndc80 complex, would have implications for how attachment strength is established and modulated by tension.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional implications of the two-ring model.

claim: The corresponding regions of Nuf2p form cross-links to the same regions of the Dam1 complex as Ndc80p.
source: The corresponding regions of Nuf2p also formed cross-links to these same regions of the Dam1 complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by cross-linking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ndc80 complexes carrying a mutation in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p demonstrate homogeneous behavior in size exclusion chromatography, similar to wild type.
source: Importantly, Ndc80 complexes carrying a mutation in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p demonstrated homogeneous behavior in size exclusion chromatography, similar to the wild type Ndc80 complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is supported by size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3E.

claim: Ndc80-GFP complex containing Ndc80p insertional mutations outside the regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p have similar microtubule and Dam1 complex binding characteristics as the wild-type Ndc80 complex.
source: Ndc80-GFP complex containing Ndc80p insertional mutations outside the regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p had similar microtubule and Dam1 complex binding characteristics as the wild-type Ndc80 complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: The insertional mutants in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p were previously identified as lethal because they disrupted the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes.
source: These observations suggest regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p each contribute to the interaction of Ndc80 complex with Dam1 complex; and the insertional mutants in these three regions were previously identified as lethal because they disrupted the interaction between the Dam1 and Ndc80 complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of lethality data from previous work (Tien et al., 2013) and the current data showing these mutations disrupt Dam1 binding.

claim: The Dam1 complex forms rings on microtubules as previously reported.
source: The Dam1 complex formed rings on microtubules as previously reported (Figure 3A,B; Miranda et al., 2005; Westermann et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy images (Figure 3A,B) and citations to previous work.

claim: The stacked double-ring organization of Dam1 complexes may be analogous to the paired ring helices previously reported to form at higher concentrations.
source: The stacked double-ring organization may be analogous to the paired ring helices previously reported to form at higher concentrations of Dam1 complex (Miranda et al., 2005).
evidence: This is speculation based on comparison with previous observations at different concentrations.

claim: In the majority of cells depleted of Ndc80 or with a mutation in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p, the SPBs are separated by more than 2 μm.
source: In addition, in the majority of cells depleted of Ndc80 or with a mutation in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, or CNdc80p the SPBs were separated by more than 2 μm (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of SPB distances shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Long spindles and high frequency of detached CEN3 suggest that few if any kinetochores are bioriented in Ndc80 mutant cells.
source: These long spindles and the high frequency of detached CEN3 suggest that few if any of the kinetochores were bioriented.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of long spindle and detachment phenotypes.

claim: Mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p have little effect on binding of Dam1 complex to microtubules.
source: These observations suggest that mutations in regions ANdc80p, BNdc80p, and CNdc80p had little effect on binding of Dam1 complex to the microtubules
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Dad4-CFP still decorates spindle microtubules in mutant cells.

claim: Single mutations in region BNdc80p or CNdc80p result in less severe defects than mutations in region ANdc80p.
source: Single mutations in region BNdc80p or CNdc80p resulted in less severe defects.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of correlation coefficients for different mutants shown in Figure 6C.
